title: Rotate a list
prompt:
Write rotate_list(items, k) that returns a new list with the items moved k places to the right; the items that fall off the end come back at the front. k can be larger than the list.
Example: ([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 2) -> [4, 5, 1, 2, 3]. The original list must not change.
hints: Try [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] with k = 1 by hand, then k = 2. What happens to the last items?
Rotating by the length of the list brings you back to the start, so rotating by 7 on a list of 3 is the same as rotating by 1. Which operator gives you the remainder?
Plan: if the list is empty return []; reduce k with k % len(items); the answer is the last k items followed by the rest. Slices like items[-k:] and items[:-k] help, but beware of k = 0.

edge_hints.empty: Taking a remainder by len(items) fails for an empty list (division by zero). Handle the empty list first.
edge_hints.zero: k = 0 means no change. Watch out: items[-0:] is the WHOLE list, not an empty one.
edge_hints.edge: Rotating by exactly the length of the list gives back the same list.
edge_hints.large: k bigger than the list: reduce it first with %.
